pagerbot: INCIDENT: GPU_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTION detected in us-west-2 — queue growth + autoscaler failing to add capacity. Paging oncall: @anya_oncall :rotating_light:

anya_oncall: seeing sustained queue length on inference-worker pool, latency spikes to 2-3s p50 -> p99 12s, elevated 5xx from router. Noted increase ~09:12 UTC.

mohit_rt: digging into autoscaler logs now. API shows scale attempts hitting `max_replicas` for pool `inference-gpu-v2`.

pagerbot: automated note: 6 customers have reported timeouts via support webhook in last 8m. Severity: Sev2.

lena_sre: adding context - we rolled continuous-batching params 06:30 UTC this morning (shrink `batch_window_ms` from 40 -> 10 and `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 128) as throughput optimisation. Suspect regression.

tao_runtime: oof, increasing `max_batch_size` while shrinking window can hurt KV/prefix cache locality. If prefix cache miss rate spikes, per-request CPU/GPU overhead goes up and autoscaler sees higher CPU usage per replica.

anya_oncall: confirm: redis prefix-cache miss rate jumped 3x after the config push. Metrics: `prefix_cache_hit_rate` dropped 0.87 -> 0.29 over 2h.

mohit_rt: autoscaler pod log snippet: ```ERROR autoscaler: attempted_scale to 24 rejected, pool cap 20
WARN autoscaler: scale failed: quota.max_replicas_reached
```

mohit_rt: we tried scale, but quota prevented new nodes. Account-level cap set by infra to 20 for this pool.

james_support: customers A and B seeing 504s and slow token streams. Support tickets up-to-date; I linked a temporary status note to the status page.

sarah_pm: prep message for affected customers: short ETA and mitigation steps. Keep promise that we're routing and investigating.

lena_sre: mitigation options: 1) increase pool cap (fast if infra approves), 2) roll back batching config to previous values, 3) enable routing to warm fallback model variant (smaller memory) to reduce GPU pressure.

tao_runtime: quick wins: revert `batch_window_ms` to 40 and cap `max_batch_size` to 64, and enable prefix cache warmup for hot prefixes. Rolling that back should lower per-replica load and let autoscaler bring queue down.

anya_oncall: starting rollback now. Command: ```kubectl set env deploy/inference-runtime BATCH_WINDOW_MS=40 MAX_BATCH_SIZE=64 --namespace=prod-us-west-2``` Applying.

pagerbot: deploybot: rolling update started for deployment inference-runtime (prod-us-west-2). 6/20 pods updated.

mohit_rt: submitting emergency request to infra slack for pool cap bump: `request:increase pool inference-gpu-v2 20->30 reason: temporary mitigation for customer impact` — pinging @infra-oncall.

infra-oncall (via DM): we see quota spike; immediate soft-allow for 2h to 28 replicas while we evaluate.

lena_sre: good. With soft-allow we should get some breathing room. Also I'm kicking off a cache-warm job to prepopulate prefix cache for highest-traffic keys: ```python scripts/warm_prefix_cache.py --top 1000 --pool inference-gpu-v2```

james_support: PASSED to customers: "We've implemented a mitigation to reduce request latency and temporarily increased capacity; we'll update when load stabilizes."

tao_runtime: monitoring KV eviction and GPU utilization. After rollback of batch params, prefix_cache_hit_rate up to 0.62 (was 0.29) within 6m. p99 latency down from 12s -> 6s. Queue length falling.

anya_oncall: autoscaler logs show additional replicas accepted now; new replicas coming up. ```INFO autoscaler: scaled pool inference-gpu-v2 20 -> 27```

pagerbot: note: alert suppression for repeated queue alerts enabled for incident channel.

lena_sre: follow-ups to do post-incident: - revert pool cap change after analysis - add guardrail to prevent batch param combos that reduce cache locality - automated test in staging for batch/cache behavior - update runbook with prefix-cache warmup step

mohit_rt: root cause hypothesis: an experimental batching config intended to improve throughput inadvertently increased working set and reduced prefix cache hit rate, causing each replica to process fewer requests per second and triggering many scale attempts until hitting pool cap. Autoscaler lacked fatigue/backoff when scale rejected, leading to queue growth.

sarah_pm: customer impact summary for postmortem: "approx 25 minutes of degraded latency and intermittent 5xx for ~6 customers; mitigated by rollback of batching params and temporary capacity increase; engineering rollback validated by metrics and warmup job."

anya_oncall: transitioning to follow-up thread. If any team needs oncall handoff, ping me. Closing incident channel in 10m when all alerts quiet. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (signals stable for 15m). Incident duration 00:47:21. Severity downgraded to SEV3 for follow-up action items.

tao_runtime: filing a short postmortem doc in /eng-runtime/incidents with timeline and proposed guardrails.

james_support: I'll add customer-facing postmortem note and flag any escalation requests.

lena_sre: thanks team. Lessons: be careful with combo changes to batching + cache behavior; add preflight job to simulate prefix cache hit rate before rollout.
